title: Edge-to-cloud architecture: from sensor boards to a dashboard
description: Choose how six classroom boards reach an MQTT broker, storage and a dashboard: direct serial, a radio relay or BLE, measured on the same seeded stub network, decided in an ADR and kept true by a fitness test.
outcome: You can state an edge pipeline's constraints as numbers, measure options for loss and latency on a seeded network, find the cause of a scaling failure (lock-step senders, not buffer size), record the decision and guard it with a test.
environment: Python 3.12 stdlib + labs/sim_stub (stub boards, radio) + labs/L400/_edge (LinkAir per-link loss, MiniBroker, SQLite store). Reuses lab 15's gateway framer and lab 12's ARQ. Optional, pending-ci: Mosquitto 2.1.2 + paho-mqtt 2.1.0; the simulator harness (Node 24, Playwright 1.64.1).
overview: Design the whole path, then measure it: the hop you did not design (here the relay's 3-frame queue) fails first, and desynchronising senders beats a bigger buffer.
prerequisites: L300 #12 A reliable radio protocol (ARQ, CRC-16)
L300 #15 A serial gateway to the PC (framing, MQTT-style output)

glossary.meaning: The micro:bit on the PC's USB port that receives radio frames, acks them and prints serial frames.
Boards that sample and retry at the same instants, so their frames always arrive together.
A small random delay added to a schedule or timeout to break lock-step.
95 % of readings reached the store within this time (nearest-rank, observed).
Architecture decision record: Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences (Nygard).
An automated test that keeps an architectural decision true as the code changes.

concepts: Constraints first, as numbers; then measure options on the same seeded run.
Shared queues fail under synchronised senders: desynchronise, then buffer.
Defaults are decisions: queue 3 and length 32 must be checked against the design.

designBrief.context: A classroom has six micro:bit V2 boards (temperature, light, motion) spread around the room and one PC (Mac mini or Windows 11) that publishes to an MQTT broker, stores readings and feeds a dashboard. MicroPython only.
constraints: >= 99 % of readings stored (6 boards, 1 reading per second, per-link radio loss 5-15 %)
p95 sensor-to-store latency <= 2,000 ms
at most 1 USB cable to the PC; boards can be moved
MicroPython on micro:bit V2 (no BLE API for user code)
designBrief.question: Which path do readings take from the boards to the store - direct serial, a radio relay, or BLE - and what must the relay design do to meet the constraints?

options.name: A. Direct serial (one USB cable per board)
options.description: Each board prints lab 15 frames on its own USB port; the gateway reads six ports.
options.evidence: options.py: 180/180 stored, p50 = p95 = 13 ms, 0 radio frames; needs 6 USB cables/ports.
options.verdict: Fastest, but fails the one-cable constraint and pins boards to the PC.

options.name: B. Radio relay -> one serial gateway
options.description: Sensors send with lab 12's ARQ to a relay board on the PC; the relay acks, dedupes and prints frames.
options.evidence: As written (node.py): 160/180 (88.9 %), p95 9,578 ms, 56 given up, 149 relay-queue drops. With random phase + jittered timeouts + queue 12 (solution.py): 180/180, p95 153 ms; 24 boards 480/480. Queue 12 without jitter, 24 boards: 151/480 (31.5 %).
options.verdict: Chosen (after the fix): meets every constraint; desynchronisation is the part that scales.

options.name: C. BLE
options.description: Boards as BLE peripherals, the PC as central.
options.evidence: Not measurable here: micro:bit MicroPython V2 implements only BLE flashing (docs); the stub has no BLE.
options.verdict: Rejected for this track; would need different firmware (e.g. MakeCode/CODAL).

fitnessFunction.what: Six sensors, five seeds, the design's loss table: delivery, p95 latency and give-ups stay within the constraints.
fitnessFunction.threshold: delivery >= 99.0 %, p95 <= 2,000 ms, gave_up == 0 for seeds 1-5

scalingLimits: Frame size: the frame carries a growing counter and timestamp; at the default 32-byte length every frame after ~1,000 s was truncated (lab 20's run). Signal: CRC rejects at the relay on one board after a fixed uptime. Fixed with length 64; a 32-bit counter in decimal still grows.

Relay CPU and UART: each forwarded frame costs a Python CRC and ~2 ms of UART at 115,200 baud (24 bytes); the stub models neither, so it shows 40 boards working. Signal: relay_queue_drops > 0 and a rising p95 as boards are added - measure on the simulator/board first.
Shared air: real radios collide when two boards transmit at once; the stub delivers both. Signal: retx rising with board count at constant link quality.

codeWalkthrough.title: One file, two roles
codeWalkthrough.detail: new_state(role, dev): the same program runs on sensors and on the relay, so a firmware update is one file. On a board, DEV comes from machine.unique_id().

codeWalkthrough.title: radio.config(group, queue=QUEUE)
codeWalkthrough.detail: The receive queue holds 3 frames by default and drops new ones when full (radio docs). With six senders that default becomes the bottleneck.

codeWalkthrough.title: sample(now) and next_sample
codeWalkthrough.detail: Each reading carries the sensor's own timestamp, so the store can compute sensor-to-store latency. next_sample starts at the same value everywhere: lock-step.

codeWalkthrough.title: first_timeout() and pump()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Lab 12's stop-and-wait ARQ: one frame in flight, doubling timeout capped at 800 ms, MAX_TRIES then gave_up. Identical timeouts keep lost frames colliding on every retry.

codeWalkthrough.title: on_frame() on the relay
codeWalkthrough.detail: Acks every copy (the last ack may have been lost), drops duplicates per device by sequence number, and prints a lab 15 frame $LLL<dev,seq,payload>*CRC for the gateway.

codeWalkthrough.title: edge_sim.run()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Seven stub boards on LinkAir (seeded per-link loss), 10 ms ticks; the relay's printed bytes go through lab 15's Framer (reused, not copied), MiniBroker QoS 1 and an SQLite store keyed on (dev, seq).

codeWalkthrough.title: solution.py
codeWalkthrough.detail: random phase per board, jittered first timeout and backoff, QUEUE 12 (~768 B RAM at length 64), LENGTH 64 so the frame survives a school day.

title: Device fleet management: versioned config over the radio
description: Give every board an identity and a config version, update configuration over the radio with acknowledgement, probation and automatic rollback, and roll out in stages - with a fitness test that no device runs an unacknowledged config.
outcome: You can design and test a two-phase, acknowledged config update with rollback, compare push-all and staged rollouts by blast radius and time, and state the invariant that keeps the fleet registry honest.
environment: Python 3.12 stdlib + labs/sim_stub (six stub boards + a gateway radio on LinkAir, 10 % loss). No new packages. Simulator run pending-ci.
overview: A config is only 'deployed' when the gateway holds an acknowledgement for it: stage, ack, commit, confirm, and let the device roll itself back when nobody confirms.
prerequisites: L400 #17 Edge-to-cloud architecture: from sensor boards to a dashboard
L300 #12 A reliable radio protocol (ack, retransmit)

glossary.meaning: A monotonically increasing integer naming one complete configuration.
Prepare (stage + ack) first, commit (apply) only after the ack was received.
After applying, the device waits for a confirmation; none in time -> roll back.
The first, small wave of a rollout, evaluated before the rest (SRE Workbook).
How many devices a bad change reaches before it is stopped.
The gateway's record of acknowledged versions per device: the source of truth.

concepts: Sent is not running: record acknowledgements, not intentions.
The device must be able to roll back alone, because a bad config can make it deaf.
Staged rollouts trade time for blast radius; probation too tight makes false rollbacks.

designBrief.context: Six deployed boards (lesson 17) need config changes over the radio: interval i (ms), temperature alarm th (C), radio group g. Links lose 10-30 % of frames. A wrong group makes a board deaf to the gateway.
constraints: no device ever runs a config version the gateway has not acknowledged (0 device-ticks)
a bad config exposes at most 1 device and never needs a physical re-flash
a good config reaches all 6 devices within 10 s at 10 % loss
device code is MicroPython; config state is small
designBrief.question: How are config updates delivered, applied and rolled back, and how are they rolled out across the fleet?

options.name: A. One-phase push to all
options.description: Device applies a config on receipt, then sends A.
options.evidence: fleet_sim.py: 12,086 unacknowledged device-ticks; v3 (group 99) left 5 devices deaf (final 333332, 120,800 device-ms); v2 done at 310 ms, 177 gateway frames.
options.verdict: Rejected: breaks the invariant and bricks devices.

options.name: B. Two-phase with probation, push to all
options.description: C -> stage, K; G -> apply, A every 500 ms; OK confirms; no OK in 3 s -> roll back, R.
options.evidence: 0 unacknowledged ticks; 4 devices ran v3 at once, 12,000 device-ms deaf, all rolled back (final 222222); v2 done at 1,210 ms; 99 frames.
options.verdict: Meets the invariant, fails the blast-radius limit.

options.name: C. Two-phase with probation, staged (canary 1 -> 2 -> 3)
options.description: Same device protocol; the gateway halts the rollout on any R, N or wave timeout.
options.evidence: 0 unacknowledged ticks; 1 device on v3, 3,000 device-ms deaf, halted after the canary; v2 done at 1,850 ms; 34 frames.
options.verdict: Chosen: meets every constraint for 640 ms more rollout time.

fitnessFunction.what: The registry invariant and the canary blast radius under loss.
fitnessFunction.threshold: unacked_ticks == 0 for 5 seeds x 10 %/30 % loss x push-all/staged; staged max_on_bad <= 1

scalingLimits: Rollout time grows with waves and retries: at 40 % loss v2 took 5,850 ms for 6 boards; for hundreds of boards, waves must run in parallel within a stage. Signal: wave timeouts (halted with phases still 'prepare').
Probation vs loss: a 300 ms probation at 30 % loss rolled back the GOOD config (tryIt). Signal: R reports for a version that later succeeds on retry - lengthen probation, repeat A.
Gateway radio airtime: every C/G/OK is a frame on the shared group; the 6-board staged rollout used 34 frames, push-all 99 - at fleet scale config traffic competes with telemetry.

codeWalkthrough.title: Config = version + validated pairs
codeWalkthrough.detail: parse_cfg() accepts exactly i, th and g, each in range, else the device answers N: a config is validated where it will run.

codeWalkthrough.title: device_id()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Identity from machine.unique_id() on the board, never a typed name; the stub falls back to 'stub' and the tests pass names.

codeWalkthrough.title: apply()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Changes the radio group if g changed: the one setting that can cut the device off from the gateway.

codeWalkthrough.title: on_message() in config_agent.py
codeWalkthrough.detail: One-phase: apply, then send A. Between the two, and forever if A is lost or the device went deaf, it runs a version nobody acknowledged.

codeWalkthrough.title: solution.py on_message()
codeWalkthrough.detail: C stages and answers K; only G for the staged version applies it, keeping last-good; OK ends probation.

codeWalkthrough.title: solution.py watchdog()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Repeats A every 500 ms during probation; no OK within 3 s -> apply last-good and send R. The device decides alone because it may be deaf.

codeWalkthrough.title: fleet.py Fleet.step()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Resends C/G every 300 ms per device in the current wave, advances waves when all confirmed, halts on R/N/timeout; acked[] is the registry the fitness test checks.

title: A digital twin of the sensor network
description: Build a model of the classroom network (Monte Carlo of the radio protocol + a room thermal model), calibrate it on gateway telemetry, compare predicted vs observed per window and choose a drift check that finds slow drift without crying wolf.
outcome: You can calibrate a simple twin on early data, turn predicted-vs-observed into z-scores, pick robust signals, and compare per-window thresholds with CUSUM by detection delay and false-alarm rate.

overview: A twin predicts what the gateway should see; drift is a small error that keeps its sign - add the evidence up (CUSUM) instead of judging one window.

code:
"""Lab 20 - digital twin of the classroom sensor network: drift check (BEFORE).

The twin (twin_model.py) predicts, per device and 30-reading window, two things the gateway can see:
  lat   the share of readings that needed a radio retransmission (from the link-loss model)
  temp  the reading minus the room model (from the thermal model + the board's calibrated offset)
and turns predicted vs observed into z-scores (observed - predicted, in model standard deviations).
This version alarms on ANY single window with |z| > Z_LIMIT. A tight limit catches drift earlier, but
every noisy window is a false alarm; the twin has no memory, so slow drift hides inside the noise.
"""
import json

import twin_model

Z_LIMIT = 2.0


class Twin:
    def __init__(self, params):
        self.params = params                 # calibrated per device: loss, offset, temp_sd
        self.alarms, self.log = [], []

    def update(self, dev, obs):
        """Feed one observed window; return the alarms it raised."""
        z = twin_model.z_scores(self.params, dev, obs)
        raised = []
        for signal in ("lat", "temp"):
            if abs(z[signal]) > Z_LIMIT:     # memoryless threshold on one window
                raised.append({"t": obs["t"], "dev": dev, "alarm": "DRIFT_" + signal.upper(),
                               "z": round(z[signal], 1)})
        self.log.append(json.dumps({"t": obs["t"], "dev": dev, "z_lat": round(z["lat"], 2),
                                    "z_temp": round(z["temp"], 2)}))
        self.alarms += raised
        return raised

code:
"""Lab 21 - local model at the gateway explains incidents and drafts the operator note (BEFORE).

Pattern from the LPC1768 guide's capstone: deterministic code raises the alarms; a local model
(Ollama on the Mac mini / Windows PC, OpenAI-compatible) explains them in plain language.
This first version trusts the model too much: it parses the reply and APPLIES any "actions" in it,
so the model - or text hidden in the data it reads - can clear an alarm the code raised.

Run:  python incident_assistant.py --fake      (deterministic fake model server, no download)
      python incident_assistant.py             (real local model: LOCAL_MODEL_URL / LOCAL_MODEL)
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent.parent / "_shared"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
import alarms as rules  # noqa: E402
import incident  # noqa: E402
from local_agent.client import chat  # noqa: E402

SYSTEM = ("You explain incidents of a classroom micro:bit sensor network to the teacher in 2-4 plain "
          "sentences. Reply only with an object {\"explanation\": \"...\", \"operator_note\": \"...\"}.")


def build_messages(snapshot, alarms):
    data = json.dumps({"alarms": alarms, "devices": snapshot["devices"]}, sort_keys=True)
    return [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
            {"role": "user", "content": "[[MICROBIT-INCIDENT]] Explain this incident:\n<incident>" + data + "</incident>"}]


def run(chat_fn, snapshot):
    alarms = rules.decide(snapshot)
    reply = json.loads(chat_fn(build_messages(snapshot, alarms)))
    for action in reply.get("actions", []):           # the model gets a WRITE path to the alarms
        if "clear_alarm" in action:
            alarms = [a for a in alarms if a["name"] != action["clear_alarm"]]
    return {"alarms": alarms, "explanation": reply.get("explanation", ""), "note": reply.get("operator_note", "")}


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--fake", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    server = None
    if args.fake:
        from local_agent import fake_model_server
        server, url = fake_model_server.start_in_thread()
        chat_fn = lambda m: chat(m, base_url=url, model="fake-model", timeout=60)   # noqa: E731
    else:
        chat_fn = lambda m: chat(m, timeout=120)                                      # noqa: E731
    try:
        out = run(chat_fn, incident.snapshot())
        print("alarms shown:", ", ".join("%s@%s" % (a["name"], a["dev"]) for a in out["alarms"]))
        print("operator note:", out["note"])
    finally:
        if server:
            server.shutdown()
            server.server_close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Capstone: classroom environmental monitor network - run it end to end and print a scorecard.

Deterministic core decides (firmware + gateway rules, verifier, twin's CUSUM, fleet registry);
the local model only explains, and code checks what it says. Prints JSON lines, one per rubric
criterion, then {"scorecard": "PASS"|"FAIL", ...}. Seeded (22); simulated time; stub boards only.
Run:  python run_capstone.py            (Windows: py run_capstone.py)   ~1 minute
"""
import json
import statistics
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
import build_firmware  # noqa: E402
import pipeline  # noqa: E402
from simnet import percentile, reuse  # noqa: E402
from store import to_csv, to_prometheus  # noqa: E402

fleet_sim = reuse("L400/18-fleet-config/fleet_sim.py", "l400_fleet_sim")
assistant = reuse("L400/21-edge-ai-explain/solution.py", "l400_assistant")
sys.path[:] = [p for p in sys.path if not any(k in p for k in ("18-fleet", "20-digital", "21-edge-ai"))]
twin_cls = reuse("L400/20-digital-twin/solution.py", "l400_twin").Twin
rules = assistant.rules
from labtest import load_lab  # noqa: E402
firmware = load_lab(str(HERE.parent / "21-edge-ai-explain"), "firmware_alarm.py")
LABELS = dict(assistant.incident.LABELS)                  # fleet registry labels; n4's carries an injection


def m1_m2_network(seed):
    res, gw, eve = pipeline.run_network(build_firmware.build(), seed=seed)
    lat = [r["t_store"] - r["t_sensor"] for r in gw.rows]
    return gw, {"sampled": res["sampled"], "stored": len(gw.rows), "p95_ms": percentile(lat, 95),
                "forged_stored": sum(r["temp"] == 45 for r in gw.rows), "replays_stored": gw.store.duplicates,
                "rejects": dict((k, sum(k in line for line in gw.verifier.log)) for k in ("mac", "replay")),
                "eve": eve.sent}


def m3_fleet(seed):
    m, _ = fleet_sim.run("solution.py", "staged", seed=seed)
    return {"unacked_ticks": m["unacked_ticks"], "max_on_bad": m["max_on_bad"],
            "final": "".join(str(v) for v in m["final"].values())}


def m4_twin(gw):
    by = {}
    for r in sorted(gw.rows, key=lambda r: (r["dev"], r["seq"])):
        by.setdefault(r["dev"], []).append(r)
    twin = twin_cls(pipeline.twin_model.calibrate(by))
    wins = dict((d, pipeline.twin_model.windows(rows)) for d, rows in by.items())
    found = {}
    for i in range(pipeline.twin_model.CALIB_WINDOWS, max(len(w) for w in wins.values())):
        for dev in sorted(wins):
            if i < len(wins[dev]):
                for a in twin.update(dev, pipeline.twin_model.observe(wins[dev][i])):
                    found["%s %s" % (a["dev"], a["alarm"])] = i
    return twin, found


def m5_alarms_and_agent(gw, twin, auth):
    by = {}
    for r in sorted(gw.rows, key=lambda r: (r["dev"], r["seq"])):
        by.setdefault(r["dev"], []).append(r)
    snap = {"devices": [{"dev": d, "label": LABELS[d], "temps": [r["temp"] for r in rows[-3:]], "readings": len(rows)}
                        for d, rows in sorted(by.items())],
            "twin_alarms": [{"dev": a["dev"], "alarm": a["alarm"], "z": a["z"]} for a in twin.alarms], "auth": auth}
    hot_fw, fw = False, {}
    for d in snap["devices"]:
        for t in by[d["dev"]][-60:]:
            hot_fw = firmware.check(fw.get(d["dev"], False), t["temp"])
            fw[d["dev"]] = hot_fw
    from local_agent import fake_model_server
    from local_agent.client import chat
    server, url = fake_model_server.start_in_thread()
    try:
        out = assistant.run(lambda m: chat(m, base_url=url, model="fake-model", timeout=60), snap)
    finally:
        server.shutdown()
        server.server_close()
    return snap, out, fw


def m6_dashboard(gw, out_dir):
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    csv_text, prom = to_csv(gw.store.rows()), to_prometheus(gw.store.summary())
    (out_dir / "dashboard.csv").write_text(csv_text, encoding="utf-8")     # Superset: Upload CSV
    (out_dir / "metrics.txt").write_text(prom, encoding="utf-8")         # Prometheus text format (text/plain)
    prom_total = sum(int(line.split()[-1]) for line in prom.splitlines() if line.startswith("classroom_readings_total{"))
    return {"csv_rows": len(csv_text.splitlines()) - 1, "prom_total": prom_total}


def scorecard(seed=pipeline.SEED, out_dir=None):
    gw, net = m1_m2_network(seed)
    fleet = m3_fleet(seed)
    twin, drift = m4_twin(gw)
    snap, agent, fw = m5_alarms_and_agent(gw, twin, net["rejects"])
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) as tmp:      # exports go to out_dir, or to a private folder
        dash = m6_dashboard(gw, Path(out_dir or tmp))
    code = rules.decide(snap)
    rows = [
        ("M1", "delivery", round(100.0 * net["stored"] / net["sampled"], 2), ">= 99.0 %", net["stored"] >= 0.99 * net["sampled"]),
        ("M1", "p95 latency ms", net["p95_ms"], "<= 2000", net["p95_ms"] <= 2000),
        ("M2", "forged/replayed readings stored", [net["forged_stored"], net["replays_stored"]], "[0, 0]",
         net["forged_stored"] == 0 and net["replays_stored"] == 0),
        ("M2", "attacks seen and rejected", net["rejects"], "mac >= 1 and replay >= 1", min(net["rejects"].values()) >= 1),
        ("M3", "unacked config ticks / canary blast radius", [fleet["unacked_ticks"], fleet["max_on_bad"]], "[0, <= 1]",
         fleet["unacked_ticks"] == 0 and fleet["max_on_bad"] <= 1 and fleet["final"] == "222222"),
        ("M4", "n5 link drift found (window)", drift.get("n5 DRIFT_LAT"), "<= 19 (drift from window 10)",
         drift.get("n5 DRIFT_LAT") is not None and drift["n5 DRIFT_LAT"] <= 19),
        ("M4", "other drift alarms", sorted(k for k in drift if k not in ("n5 DRIFT_LAT", "n4 DRIFT_TEMP")), "<= 1 entry",
         len([k for k in drift if k not in ("n5 DRIFT_LAT", "n4 DRIFT_TEMP")]) <= 1),
        ("M5", "TEMP_HIGH n4 by gateway and firmware", [any(a["name"] == "TEMP_HIGH" and a["dev"] == "n4" for a in code), fw.get("n4")],
         "[true, true]", any(a["name"] == "TEMP_HIGH" and a["dev"] == "n4" for a in code) and fw.get("n4") is True),
        ("M5", "model cannot change alarms", agent["digest"] == rules.freeze(code)[1] and not agent["accepted"],
         "digest equal; injected reply rejected", agent["digest"] == rules.freeze(code)[1] and not agent["accepted"]),
        ("M6", "dashboard exports match the store", [dash["csv_rows"], dash["prom_total"], net["stored"]], "all equal",
         dash["csv_rows"] == dash["prom_total"] == net["stored"]),
    ]
    lines = [json.dumps({"milestone": m, "criterion": c, "value": v, "threshold": t, "pass": bool(p)}) for m, c, v, t, p in rows]
    passed = sum(bool(r[4]) for r in rows)
    lines.append(json.dumps({"scorecard": "PASS" if passed == len(rows) else "FAIL", "passed": passed, "total": len(rows),
                             "operator_note": agent["note"][:120] + "..."}))
    return lines, {"net": net, "fleet": fleet, "drift": drift, "agent": agent, "dash": dash,
                   "mean_temp": round(statistics.fmean(r["temp"] for r in gw.rows), 2)}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for line in scorecard(out_dir=HERE / "out")[0]:
        print(line)
